pick.headline: Rios Montt takes power in Guatemalan coup
pick.summary: On March 23, 1982, junior officers in Guatemala staged a coup that brought General Efrain Rios Montt to power.
pick.significance: His seventeen months in power saw the bloodiest phase of the counterinsurgency against the Maya highlands.
pick.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of March 24, 1982, listed under Guatemala a full sequence on the coup by "Young Officers": army communiques claiming control, the Lucas Garcia government's resignation, a junta suspending Congress and the constitution, and Rios Montt addressing the nation; Mexico and Costa Rica deplored it.

alternates.headline: Reagan announces the Strategic Defense Initiative
alternates.summary: On March 23, 1983, President Reagan proposed a program to develop defences that would make nuclear missiles obsolete.
alternates.significance: The 'Star Wars' initiative alarmed Moscow and became a central obstacle and bargaining chip in arms talks.

alternates.headline: Mexican presidential candidate Colosio assassinated
alternates.summary: On March 23, 1994, Luis Donaldo Colosio, presidential candidate of Mexico's ruling PRI, was shot dead at a rally in Tijuana.
alternates.significance: The killing, after the Chiapas uprising, deepened Mexico's political crisis in a year that ended in financial collapse.
